solution_steps.name: conductance
solution_steps.explain: conductivity is the reciprocal of resistance

solution_steps.name: half_resistance_current
solution_steps.explain: current if the wire were half as resistive

questions.q: A copper wire of resistance 4 ohm is connected to a 12 V battery. Taking conductivity as the reciprocal of resistance, find the conductance and the current in the wire.
questions.a: 3 A

questions.q: An aluminium rod has resistance 8 ohm. It is placed across 24 V. Compute its conductance and the current it carries.
questions.a: 3 A

questions.q: A graphite rod of resistance 10 ohm is put across a 5 V cell. Find its conductance in siemens and the current flowing.
The heating element of a toaster has resistance 20 ohm at working temperature and is run on 110 V. What current does it draw?
A thick silver wire has a very low resistance of 2 ohm. Connected to 9 V, what current flows through it?
Why do metals conduct electricity well?
questions.a: They contain free, mobile electrons that drift when a potential difference is applied.

questions.q: Why are metals sonorous and lustrous?
questions.a: Their closely packed metallic lattice rings on striking (sonority) and free electrons reflect light, giving a shine.

questions.q: State two physical properties in which non-metals differ from metals.
questions.a: Non-metals are poor conductors (except graphite) and are brittle or soft, often dull, and not sonorous.

questions.q: How do sodium and potassium differ from magnesium towards water?
questions.a: Sodium and potassium react vigorously with cold water catching fire; magnesium reacts slowly with hot water only.

questions.q: Why is calcium left floating when put in water?
questions.a: Hydrogen bubbles stick to it and the reaction heat keeps it afloat as it reacts.

questions.q: Which metals do not react with water even as steam?
questions.a: Less reactive metals like lead, copper, silver and gold do not displace hydrogen from water or steam.

questions.q: What does the reactivity series tell us?
questions.a: It arranges metals from most to least reactive, predicting which metal displaces another from its salt solution.

questions.q: Why can silver not displace hydrogen from dilute acids?
questions.a: Silver lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot push hydrogen out of acids.

questions.q: A metal X displaces zinc from zinc sulphate but not magnesium from magnesium sulphate. Where does it sit?
questions.a: X is more reactive than zinc but less reactive than magnesium, so it lies between magnesium and zinc.

questions.q: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?
questions.a: Strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions need large energy to break.

questions.q: Why do ionic compounds conduct electricity in molten state or solution but not as solids?
questions.a: In the solid, ions are fixed in the lattice; melting or dissolving frees the ions to move and carry current.

questions.q: Are ionic compounds generally soluble in water or in kerosene?
questions.a: In water (polar solvent) they dissolve; in organic solvents like kerosene they do not.

questions.q: What is roasting of a sulphide ore?
questions.a: Heating the ore strongly in excess air, converting sulphides to oxides and giving out sulphur dioxide.

questions.q: How is calcination different from roasting?
questions.a: Calcination heats carbonate ores in limited air without oxygen to convert them to oxides; roasting is for sulphide ores in excess air.

questions.q: Write what happens when zinc carbonate is calcined.
questions.a: It decomposes to zinc oxide with carbon dioxide driven off.

questions.q: How does electrolytic refining of copper work?
questions.a: Impure copper is the anode, pure copper the cathode, copper sulphate solution the electrolyte; copper dissolves from the anode and deposits pure on the cathode.

questions.q: Where do the impurities of impure copper go during refining?
questions.a: Less reactive impurities settle below the anode as anode mud; reactive ones stay in solution.

questions.q: Which electrode loses mass during the refining?
questions.a: The anode, the impure copper block, dissolves away and loses mass.

questions.q: A bangle is stamped 22 carat. What per cent of it is pure gold?
An old ring is 18 carat gold. Calculate its percentage purity.
A chain marked 14 carat is bought second hand. What is its gold content in per cent?
A coin is declared 24 carat. What per cent purity does this show?
A pendant is only 12 carat. Express its gold purity as a percentage.
What is an amalgam?
questions.a: An alloy in which one of the metals is mercury.

questions.q: Why is pure gold not used for ornaments?
questions.a: Pure gold (24 carat) is very soft; it is alloyed with silver, copper or other metals to make it hard and durable.

questions.q: Name the constituents of stainless steel and one advantage of it.
questions.a: Iron with nickel and chromium; it resists rusting and is strong and shiny.
